raw_case_text: A 22-month-old girl presented to us with 8-day fever (40 C), and mild cough. On examination, she had hepatosplenomegaly. Past medical history included failure to thrive, but normal neurological development. She was the first child of a non-consanguineous marriage. She had normal brown hair and normal skin. There was no family history of albinism. On physical examination, she was stunted, pale, and had non-tender hepatomegaly of 5-6 cm; the spleen was palpable 4 cm below the left costal margin as confirmed by abdominal ultrasound. The WBC count was 5100/mm3 (ANC 1200/mm3), Hb 9.1 g/dl, and platelets 47.000/mm3. She had mild hypertransaminasemia and hypoalbuminemia. Ferritin was 1134 ng/ml. Soluble IL-2 receptor (sCD25) was 3183 UI/ml. Blood cultures were negative. Serum immunoglobulins and lymphocyte subsets were normal. Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) serology yielded seroreactivity (positive IgM and IgG anti-VCA) with negative IgG anti-EBNA. EBV viral load was 637 copies/ml. Leishmania serology showed both negative immunochromatography and indirect immunofluorescence. Conversely, serum ELISA was slightly positive. Leishmanial antigen in the urine was negative. Bone marrow aspiration revealed hemophagocytosis. The patient worsened clinically, with persistent malaise, progressive splenomegaly, and petechial rash on her chest and legs. Subsequent investigations were WBC 4800/mm3 (ANC 800/mm3), Hb 6.8 g/dl and platelets 27000/mm3, triglycerides 686 mg/dl, ferritin 3849 ng/ml, and sCD25 3596 UI/ml with normal clotting tests as well as perforin expression by flow-cytometry. Hair microscopy was not performed because clinical features of albinism were not present neither in our patient nor in her family. HLH-2004 protocol was started. The following day, Leishmania Polymerase Chain Reaction was done where Leishmanial DNA was detected by nested PCR.) This was confirmed on a bone marrow aspirate as well. Standard therapy with liposomal amphotericin B (3 mg/kg/day IV on days 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 14, and 21) was given. The patient completed HLH-2004 protocol, except for 2 doses of etoposide due to clinical and laboratory improvement without evidence of underlying primary HLH. At 30 month follow up, there is no evidence of relapse. As CD107a degranulation assay was not performed (just normal intracytoplasmic pattern of perforin staining), primary HLH is not absolutely discarded as a differential diagnosis.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 22-month-old female presented with high fever (40 °C) and mild cough for 8 days.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 22-month-old girl presented with an 8-day history of high fever up to 40 °C and mild cough. During hospitalization, she deteriorated clinically with persistent malaise, progressive splenomegaly, and a new petechial rash on her chest and legs. Laboratory testing demonstrated worsening cytopenias, hyperferritinemia, and hypertriglyceridemia, fulfilling criteria for hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH). Protocol HLH-2004 was initiated. Subsequent molecular testing established an underlying parasitic infection, and targeted antileishmanial therapy was instituted.
subjective.past_medical_history: First child of non-consanguineous parents. Past history of failure to thrive with normal neurological development. Normal brown hair and skin; no family history of albinism. Prior antibiotic therapy not documented.
subjective.review_of_systems: High-grade fever, mild cough, progressive malaise, petechial rash on trunk and legs. Denied vomiting, diarrhea, seizures, or jaundice.

objective.physical_examination: Stunted and pale infant; body temperature: 40 °C. Abdominal exam revealed non-tender hepatomegaly measuring 5-6 cm and splenomegaly palpable 4 cm below the left costal margin. Developing petechial rash on chest and lower extremities. Brown hair, normal skin pigmentation; no features of albinism.
objective.routine_investigations: Initial labs: WBC 5,100/mm^3 (ANC 1,200/mm^3), hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL, platelets 47,000/mm^3; mild hypertransaminasemia, hypoalbuminemia; serum ferritin 1,134 ng/mL; soluble IL-2 receptor (sCD25) 3,183 UI/mL. Blood cultures: negative. Normal immunoglobulins and lymphocyte subsets. EBV serology: positive IgM and IgG anti-VCA, negative IgG anti-EBNA; EBV viral load 637 copies/mL. Repeat labs during clinical deterioration: WBC 4,800/mm^3 (ANC 800/mm^3), hemoglobin 6.8 g/dL, platelets 27,000/mm^3, triglycerides 686 mg/dL, ferritin 3,849 ng/mL, sCD25 3,596 UI/mL; normal coagulation tests. Flow cytometry: normal intracytoplasmic perforin expression. Urine parasite antigen: negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal ultrasonography confirmed hepatomegaly (5-6 cm) and splenomegaly (4 cm below costal margin). Bone marrow aspiration revealed prominent hemophagocytosis. Leishmania serology: immunochromatography and indirect immunofluorescence negative; serum ELISA weakly positive.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive Diagnosis: Visceral leishmaniasis (VL) triggering secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH), with concurrent low-level EBV reactivation.
Diagnostic Confirmation: Detection of Leishmania DNA by nested PCR from peripheral blood and bone marrow aspirate.
Differentials Ruled Out: Primary (familial) HLH (normal perforin expression, though CD107a degranulation assay not done), Griscelli syndrome and Chédiak-Higashi syndrome (normal hair and skin pigmentation, no albinism), acute bacterial sepsis (sterile blood cultures), and primary EBV-induced HLH.
Treatment & Clinical Course: Patient initiated on HLH-2004 protocol. Following PCR confirmation, standard intravenous liposomal amphotericin B (3 mg/kg/day on days 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 14, and 21) was administered. Completed HLH-2004 protocol with omission of the final 2 doses of etoposide due to rapid clinical and laboratory recovery. The patient remains in complete remission without relapse at 30-month follow-up.
